title: Two clocks
sub: How long the capital waited for its return - 1840s railways against today's compute
src: Campbell (2012), Explorations in Economic History; Odlyzko (2010) - via the research lane; compute ~5 years on the operator's word
src_full: Railways: after the 1845-47 Mania, dividends took the subsequent two decades to barely return to pre-Mania levels (Campbell 2012, EEH 49(2), p. 238, doi:10.1016/j.eeh.2011.10.001); the 1846 projection of GBP 560M capital earning ~5% arrived in 1872, 26 years later (Odlyzko 2010, p. 181). Compute: about five years, accepted on the operator's word 2026-09-22.

proof.quote: During the subsequent two decades the rises in dividends were modest and rates barely returned to their pre-Mania levels.
total capital investment reached £ 560 million in 1872, 26 years later
We don't need an exact source, 5 years is the fab build out
Railway steel sat waiting twenty years while the economy caught up. That's why the return took two decades. Today's compute doesn't sit. It depreciates in about five years.
